Subject: Checkout spikes — several 10s of seconds tail during peak

Hi Michael / Monica,

We're seeing spikes in response times during our morning checkout window (around 09:00–10:00 PT). Most requests are fine, but ~1.6% of requests are taking 12–28s and failing at the browser level. Error rate also nudged up from 0.2% to ~1.9% during the window. This is causing serious checkout abandonment for some users.

Attached is a small sample of request-level timing (tail_samples.csv) and a snapshot of the failing traces. We haven't changed client code. We only bumped concurrency on our end last week to handle a seasonal promotion.

Can Redwood triage? This is high-severity for our conversion metric — appreciate a prompt look.

Thanks,
Adam
Adam Carter
Head of Platform
ZenCart

On Thu, Sep 14, 2028 at 09:12 AM Adam Carter <adam.carter@zencart.com> wrote:
> We're seeing spikes ...

Thanks for the signal. Quick hypotheses from initial telemetry:
1) Concurrency cap ripple: we see per-account concurrency controls that can flip into a backpressure mode when request burst exceeds pooled tokens; some requests queue and then expire at client timeouts — that matches the long tails.
2) KV-cache thrashing: at high interleaving of prompts/seq lengths we observe KV cache eviction pressure leading to occasional re-computation spikes.
3) Hot-shard contention: small probability but possible if routing collides on a sub-pool.

What I need from ZenCart: service-side request IDs and the full request timestamps. From our side, I'll run a short diagnostic sweep (attached diagnostics-run.sh) to extract per-pool queue depth, kernel scheduling backlog, and eviction counters for the last 24h.

Short-term mitigations to propose (if confirmed):
- Apply a temporary strict route-level concurrency cap for ZenCart's high-throughput routes to prevent queue amplification (will reduce tail risk but may reduce peak RPS slightly).
- Enable route-level prefix caching for the most common checkout prompt sequences.
- Prioritize ZenCart traffic on a secondary higher-throughput pool for the next 24–48h while we dig in.

I'll post results of the sweep in this thread.

—Rishi
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: diagnostics-run.sh (script)
